findings.summary: Stale marker with no pid file never clears. If a full-scope run crashes between mkdirSync(dir) and writeFileSync(pid), exclusiveHeld returns true forever (pid null, dir exists). acquireExclusive only reclaims when holder is non-null and not alive, so it sleeps forever. Every later verify, and the pre-push hook with its unbounded wait, would hang. Consider reclaiming a pid-less marker once its mtime is older than a few seconds.

findings.summary: Time-of-check/time-of-use race between a normal acquirer and the exclusive one. A normal acquirer can pass exclusiveHeld (false) just before the exclusive run creates the marker. The exclusive run can then scan listVerifySlots before that acquirer's tryTake lands, so both run and the one-full-suite guarantee is briefly broken. Re-checking exclusiveHeld after tryTake, or re-scanning after a short settle, would close it. The dead-holder reclaim has a similar small race between two reclaimers.

findings.summary: Liveness issue, not a security vulnerability. If a full-scope holder dies after mkdirSync(dir) and before writeFileSync of the pid file, the exclusive directory is left with no pid file. exclusiveHeld then returns true forever, and acquireExclusive sleeps forever because readPid returns null and the dead-holder reclaim never runs. With SLOT_WAIT_MS = Infinity in scripts/pre-push-patch-coverage.mjs, every verify and pre-push coverage run on the host would hang until the directory is deleted by hand. Only a local crash triggers it. Consider reclaiming a pid-less marker once its mtime passes a short grace period.
